messages:
Eli: Quick day-2 checkpoint for kernel + KV prefetch work — post-stand summary. pulling owners for next milestones.

Maya: thanks. quick ask: are we still on track to flip the continuous-batching flag for canary tomorrow?

Eli: tentative yes. Carlos finishing the kernel change that avoids the extra memcpy, then Jun's KV warmup patch needs one more perf run. if both land we can canary.

Carlos: PR up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/803 — kernel memcpy removal + a small refactor. bench on p3.2x shows ~6% tail-latency improvement for seq_len 1024. ~~noted one regression in microbench for batch=1, investigating.

Jun: KV warmup PR ready for review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/792 — prefetch window heuristic + metrics. I saw the microbench regression Carlos mentioned; looks like a cold-kv race in our test harness. adding a test fix now.

Priya: heads-up: SLO burn rate could spike if we misconfigure batch sizing during canary. suggest enabling gradual ramp: start at 5% traffic, 20% after 2h, 50% after 6h if no regressions.

Eli: agreed. Maya, can the rollout policy in console be set to that? also need a fallback model-variant pinned in routing (cpu-fallback) if latency > 400ms.

Maya: yep — I'll create the rollout in console and attach the canary policy. adding the cpu-fallback route now.

Carlos: repro note: the memcpy regression only shows with kernel compiled with AVX512 disabled (older infra). maybe our kernel auto-detect path picks a slower codepath on some instances. fixing selector logic in the PR.

Jun: test fix pushed. also added a tiny histogram metric kv.prefetch.prefill_ms so we can watch warmup durations in the canary.

Eli: ownership: Carlos -> kernel selector + PR merge. Jun -> KV warmup + metrics. Maya -> rollout + routing. Priya -> monitoring + SLO thresholds. I'll coordinate canary timeline and ops pings.

Carlos: pinging @Maya for a quick config question: when can the canary be scheduled? I need the fleet to have the newer kernel-build available (image tag: runtime-kernel-20270313).

Maya: can do tomorrow 09:30 PT — I'll stamp images tonight and schedule.

Priya: I'll pre-create the alert runbook and add an automated rollback if p50>200ms for 10m or p95>350ms for 5m. also enabling trace sampling at +2x during canary.

Eli: thanks. small blockers: a) one unresolved review comment on Carlos's PR re: buffer ownership b) Jun's regen of test vectors still flaky in CI. we should not block canary on nonblocking CI flakes but want green before merge if possible.

Carlos: addressing the buffer comment now, should be done in an hour.

Jun: I'll re-run vectorgen and send an async note if CI keeps failing. if we hit flakes we can run the perf job on the canary infra manually.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: canary runtime-kernel-20270313 -> cluster:us-west-2 at 2027-03-14T16:30:00Z (09:30 PT). Rollout policy: 5%/2h/20% -> 50% -> 100%. Fallback routing enabled.

Eli: final asks before merge: Carlos — leave a short changelog blurb with expected perf impact and any infra caveats. Jun — attach the histogram dashboards to the PR. Maya/Priya — confirm rollout document link in thread when done.

Maya: added rollout doc: https://redwood-internal/docs/runbooks/continuous-batch-canary-20270313. I'll drop the link here after validation.

Priya: runbook link added to deploy ticket and I've invited on-call to monitor 2x for first 4h.

Eli: perfect. thanks all — will check back after images are stamped. :thumbsup:
